sentences.text: The evidence is mixed: a dedicated discharge coordinator improved some aspects of discharge quality but not others.

In an intervention study of 600 randomly sampled adults discharged home from three medical wards, quality of discharge planning was assessed before and after introducing a district discharge planning policy/checklist and then a discharge coordinator over three phases spanning 18 months.

After the discharge coordinator was introduced, the discharge planning process improved, patients had fewer problems after discharge, and they reported less perceived need for medical and healthcare services, but there was no evidence of more timely or effective community services or improved appropriateness/efficiency of bed use.

No, clinician assessment was not accurate enough in this study, resting on a physician sensitivity of only 39% for predicting acute chest syndrome. Among 73 patients with sickle cell disease and 96 febrile events (temperature at least 38°C) evaluated before chest radiography, 24% (23/96) had radiographic acute chest syndrome, but 61% (14/23) of those cases were not clinically suspected by the evaluating physician. No symptom or physical examination finding except splinting (4/23 versus 0/73) helped identify acute chest syndrome, 57% of acute chest syndrome patients had completely normal physical examinations, and diagnostic accuracy did not improve significantly with increasing pediatric training.

Yes, the evidence supports that hypotensive events can be followed by myocardial ischaemic events in patients with ischaemic heart disease, with 14 hypotension-induced ischaemic events occurring in 8 of 25 patients and ST events significantly associated with preceding hypotensive events (chi2=40.2, p<0.0001).
The study enrolled 25 patients with angina on one or more hypotensive cardiovascular medications and documented hypotension, recording 107 hypotensive events and 40 ST events in 14 patients.

Among the 14 hypotension-induced ischaemic events, 13 were preceded by a fall in diastolic pressure (median 57.5 mm Hg, IQR 11) and 6 by a fall in systolic pressure, and patients with these events were more often on multiple hypotensive drug regimens (8/8 vs 9/17, p=0.022).
Because this was an observational study, it demonstrates a strong temporal association but does not definitively prove causation.

The evidence is mixed but suggestive that perforation of the appendix is a risk factor for tubal infertility and possibly ectopic pregnancy, based on a review reporting elevated risk estimates but weakened by bias and confounding. The review included 23 retrieved articles, of which only 4 presented original data with nonexposed control groups. It reported risk estimates ranging from 1.6 (95% CI 1.1 to 2.5) for ectopic pregnancy after appendectomy to 4.8 (95% CI 1.5 to 14.9) for tubal infertility from perforation of the appendix. However, recall bias and poor adjustment for confounding variables in some reports weakened the validity of these studies.
Yes, this single retrospective study suggests outcome can be predicted from respiratory parameters in children with malignancy and ARDS.
In 17 children (aged 10.5 ± 5.1 years) with ARDS and malignancy, 6 (35.3%) survived, and sepsis syndrome was present in 70.6%.

Peak inspiratory pressure, positive end-expiratory pressure, and ventilation index values could distinguish outcome by day 3, while efficiency of oxygenation (PaO2/FIO2 and P(A-a)O2) related to outcome from day 8 after mechanical ventilation onset.
The finding rests on episodes being consistent (all manic or all mixed) in significantly more patients than would be expected by chance.

Over an 11-year period, the observed distribution of 1,224 manic and mixed episodes in 241 patients with three or more entries in a community mental health center management information system was compared with an expected distribution from 1,000 random simulations.
The observed consistency exceeded chance, supporting that the manic/mixed episode distinction tends to run true over time.
The NIHSS has 42 possible points, with 7 directly related to language compared with only 2 related to neglect.

In the placebo arm of the NINDS t-PA stroke trial, right hemisphere strokes had statistically greater infarct volumes than left hemisphere strokes after adjusting for baseline NIHSS (P<0.001), and for each 5-point NIHSS category below 20, median right-hemisphere volumes were about double left-hemisphere volumes.
For example, at a 24-hour NIHSS of 16 to 20, the median left-hemisphere infarct volume was 48 mL versus 133 mL for right-hemisphere strokes (P<0.001).
This means left hemisphere strokes can produce similar NIHSS scores with smaller infarcts, consistent with the scale favoring left-hemisphere deficits.
The only supplied study surveyed attitudes, not concussion outcomes, among 63 players from four Canadian teams and their coaches.
It found that 62% of players believed headgear could prevent concussion, while only 33% of coaches were convinced.
The evidence is mixed: delay in transfer to a rehabilitation ward was associated with longer total hospital length of stay but not with discharge to a more dependent residence.
In an observational study of 455 patients aged over 75 years with fracture of the proximal femur, 58% were transferred to a rehabilitation ward.
Each day of delay in transfer was associated with an additional 0.64 days of total hospital length of stay (95% CI 0.23-1.05).

For discharge to a more dependent residence among transferred patients, only age predicted outcome, with people over 85 having a relative risk of 1.47 (95% CI 1.15-1.88) compared with younger patients, not delay.
Yes, receipt of hospice care in nursing homes was associated with better management of daily pain near the end of life.

In a retrospective cohort of nursing home residents with daily pain near death, 51% of hospice residents versus 33% of nonhospice residents received regular treatment for daily pain, and after controlling for clinical confounders hospice residents were about twice as likely to receive regular treatment (adjusted OR = 2.08, 95% CI = 1.68-2.56).

Hospice residents were also less likely to receive no analgesics (15% vs 23%; OR = 0.57, 95% CI = 0.45-0.74) and less likely to receive analgesics not recommended by AMDA (21% vs 29%; OR = 0.65, 95% CI = 0.52-0.80).
Yes—mossy fibers release GABA, based on monosynaptic GABAA receptor-mediated synaptic signals recorded in CA3 pyramidal neurons after recruiting dentate granule cells.

The evidence comes from hippocampal slices from 3- to 5-week-old guinea pigs, with whole-cell voltage clamp recordings from CA3 pyramidal cells and stimulating electrodes in stratum granulosum to recruit mossy fiber-CA3 projections.

These inhibitory signals satisfied mossy fiber-CA3 criteria (high sensitivity to metabotropic glutamate-receptor agonists, facilitation during repetitive stimulation, and NMDA receptor-independent long-term potentiation), and mossy fiber terminals also showed intense GABA and GAD67 immunoreactivity.
The passages report no sample sizes, comparison group, or numerical effect sizes for these findings.
The evidence does not support hepatitis G virus or TT virus as major specific causes of cryptogenic chronic liver disease.

In 23 patients with cryptogenic chronic liver disease versus 40 with hepatitis C virus-related chronic liver disease, hepatitis G virus RNA was detected in 4/23 (17.4%) versus 6/40 (15%), a nonsignificant difference.

At least one marker of hepatitis G virus infection was present in 6/23 (26.1%) versus 16/40 (40%), also nonsignificant, and TT virus DNA was found in only 1 cryptogenic patient and 2 hepatitis C virus patients.

Demographic and clinical features, including liver histology, were comparable between hepatitis G virus-infected and uninfected subjects, while severe liver damage was more frequent in hepatitis C virus disease.
Yes, pain appears to be a clinically relevant problem in general adult psychiatry, based on its high prevalence and associated impairment and unfitness for work.

In a cross-sectional questionnaire study of 106 patients primarily diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder in general adult psychiatry, the point prevalence of pain was about 50%, the 6-month prevalence was 75.5%, and the 12-month prevalence was 76.5%.
The most frequent complaints were low back pain, headache, and shoulder and neck pain.
Almost 10% of all patients reported pain continuing at least 3 months in the past year, and impairment and unfitness for work were related to specific psychiatric diagnosis.
Statistically significant risk factors for pain were depression (OR=6.05) and the number of past admissions to psychiatric hospitals (OR=3.609).
Yes, CT can help predict the level of CSF block in tuberculous hydrocephalus, but only via the shape of the third ventricle.

In 50 children with communicating and 34 with non-communicating hydrocephalus classified by air-encephalography, the only CT finding that correlated with the type of hydrocephalus was third ventricle shape.
Significantly more children with non-communicating hydrocephalus had a rounded third ventricle than those with communicating hydrocephalus.
Yes, a 2-day course was followed by increased self-assessed communication security and reported behavior changes in communicating with terminally ill patients.

The first three courses included 31 participants who rated their security in seven communication settings before, immediately after, and 3 months after the course, with important increases for communicating cancer diagnosis, recurrence, or advanced disease without curative approach.
Three months later, participants described multiple changes indicating increased sensitivity and professionalism in communication behavior.
Yes—radiotherapy around the time of pregnancy appears to increase the risk of breast cancer in women treated for Hodgkin's disease.
The evidence comes from 382 women treated with radiotherapy for Hodgkin's disease, comparing those who received radiotherapy around pregnancy with those who were not pregnant.
Overall breast cancer incidence was 16.0% vs 2.3% (p=0.0001), and 10- and 15-year actuarial rates were 6.7% and 32.6% vs 0.4% and 1.7%, respectively.

In multivariate analysis, pregnancy around radiotherapy was the only variable associated with increased breast cancer risk, and radiotherapy during pregnancy or within 1 month of pregnancy had a hazard ratio of 22.49 (95% CI 5.56-90.88, p<0.001) compared with nonpregnant women and those irradiated later than 1 month after pregnancy.
No, higher rates of depression in women are not accounted for by differential symptom reporting in this study.

In a population-based 13-year follow-up of 1,727 community-dwelling adults in East Baltimore, women and men did not significantly differ in self-reported depression symptoms across the nine symptom groups for major depression after adjustment for age, ethnicity, education, marital status, and employment.
For example, the adjusted direct effect of gender on report of sadness was 0.105 (95% CI -0.113 to 0.323), not significantly different from the null.
Thus, the evidence indicates that differential symptom reporting does not explain the higher depression rates in women.

In 17 adult blunt trauma patients (Injury Severity Score ≥18), neutrophils migrated significantly more to interleukin-8 (30 and 100 ng/mL) at admission and 8 and 24 hrs later than neutrophils from 9 normal volunteers (p<.05).
Neutrophil counts were also elevated at admission and declined over 24 hrs in patients who later developed ARDS.
However, this was a prospective observational study, and the authors only hypothesized that enhanced migration may be crucial in ARDS etiology, so it does not prove causation.
Yes, the evidence supports c-Kit-dependent growth as a potential therapeutic target in uveal melanoma.

In 134 paraffin-embedded uveal melanomas and eight fresh-frozen samples, c-kit was expressed in 84/134 and 6/8, respectively, and cultured uveal melanoma cell lines showed strong c-kit expression and tyrosine phosphorylation compared with cutaneous melanoma cells.

The three uveal melanoma cell lines also expressed c-kit ligand, suggesting autocrine/paracrine stimulation, and treatment with STI571 blocked c-kit autophosphorylation and caused cell death with an IC50 below 2.5 microM for both phosphorylation and proliferation.
The evidence is mixed: reduced arm spasticity was associated with improved arm function in some botulinum toxin dose groups but not others.

In a pooled analysis of individual data from stroke patients in two randomized controlled trials of intramuscular botulinum toxin, maximum change in spasticity and maximum change in arm function were related independent of treatment (rho = -0.2822, p = 0.0008, n = 137).

The relationship was clear for patients treated with botulinum toxin (Dysport) at 500 or 1000 units (rho = -0.5679, p = 0.0090, n = 22; rho = -0.4430, p = 0.0018, n = 47), but not for placebo or 1500 units.
Timing was also mixed: changes were concurrent in 47 patients, spasticity improvement preceded function in 26, and function improvement preceded spasticity in 18.

The evidence is insufficient to conclude that adding 2-methoxyestradiol (2ME) can reduce chemotherapeutic dosages in the treatment of human ovarian cancer, because the available data are only from in vitro cell-line experiments.

In two human ovarian cancer cell lines, 2ME (0.8–25 microM) combined with various chemotherapeutics produced a significant additive inhibitory effect on proliferation with epirubicine and carboplatin at the lower concentration range of those chemotherapeutics.

No, this study found that higher private referral rates did not reduce NHS demand; instead, NHS referral rates were higher in wards with the highest private referral rates. Among 17,137 GP referrals from 10 UK practices in 2001, 90.4% were to the NHS and 9.6% to the private sector. After adjustment for deprivation and practice, the NHS referral rate was significantly higher in wards in the top fifth for private referral rates than in the bottom fifth (rate ratio 1.40, 95% CI 1.15 to 1.71, p=0.001). This is an observational comparison, so it shows an association rather than proving that increased private use causes NHS demand to fall.

Yes—preoperative tracheobronchoscopy mattered in newborns with esophageal atresia, being clinically useful in 28 of 62 patients (45.2%) and crucial in modifying the surgical approach in 15 of 62 (24.2%).

In a 1997–2003 series of 62 newborns with EA, preoperative TBS found unsuspected proximal fistula in 3 of 9 type A patients (reclassified as type B), plus 2 H-type fistulas and 4 previously undetected respiratory tree malformations.
It also allowed Fogarty catheter occlusion of carinal fistulas in 14 type C patients to improve ventilation during repair, with no complications observed.
The study does not compare TBS with no TBS, so it shows diagnostic and surgical impact but not comparative outcome benefit.
In 500 adverse reports, 15 algorithms were compared with WHO global introspection, using 'possible' as the lower limit for drug-relatedness.
The algorithms had high sensitivity (average 93%, PPV 89%) but low specificity (average 7%, NPV 31%).
This low specificity means they poorly identified non-drug-related reports, so they would not be a reliable substitute for global introspection.
Evidence is mixed: bile duct sludge differed from common bile duct stones in frequency and some associations, but not in recurrence after endoscopic clearance.

In 228 patients undergoing ERCP for suspected choledocholithiasis, sludge without stones occurred in 14% (31/228), was more common in females, and was less often associated with CBD dilation than stones.
After endoscopic clearance, recurrent CBD stones occurred in 16% (5/31) of sludge patients versus 17% (33/197) of stone patients (p = 0.99), and other risk factors did not differ statistically.
The evidence is mixed: French lay people and psychologists found breaching confidentiality to protect a patient's wife from an STD much more acceptable than physicians did.
In a French study, 144 lay people, 10 psychologists, and 7 physicians rated acceptability across 48 scenarios.
Mean acceptability ratings were 11.76 for lay people, 9.28 for psychologists, and 2.90 for physicians on a 0–22 scale.

Among lay participants, cluster analysis found some who considered it always acceptable (n = 14), some depending on circumstances (n = 87), some requiring expert consultation (n = 30), and some never acceptable (n = 13).
The patient's stated intentions to protect and inform his wife had the greatest impact on acceptability.
Applying the best quartile of process of care to patients currently receiving poor process was associated with a 4.24-point increment in change in SF-12 physical component summary scores.
The evidence is mixed: a statistically significant but clinically weak relationship was found, while the difference across ACE quartiles was not significant.
In 300 people with Type 1 diabetes not taking renin-angiotensin system blockers, the incidence of severe hypoglycaemia was 0.93 episodes per patient year.

The mean incidence of severe hypoglycaemia in the top versus bottom quartiles of ACE activity was 0.5 versus 1.7 episodes per patient year, but this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.075).

Spearman's test showed a very weak but statistically significant association between serum ACE and severe hypoglycaemia incidence (r = 0.115, P = 0.047), and a negative binomial model also showed a statistically significant but clinically weak relationship (P = 0.002).

No, the available evidence suggests endoaortic balloon occlusion is not safe for surgical management of the atherosclerotic ascending aorta, as it was independently associated with in-hospital death (odds ratio 5.609, 95% CI 2.684–11.719).
In a series of 2,172 consecutive patients, endoaortic occlusion was used in 52 patients selected by preoperative aortic calcifications or intraoperative epiaortic ultrasonography.
In-hospital death occurred in 25% of the endoaortic occlusion group versus 4.2% of all other patients (p<0.0001) and exceeded the expected 10.5% by EUROSCORE (p=0.05).
The balloon had to be replaced by conventional cross-clamping in 19.2% due to incomplete occlusion, hindered exposure, or balloon rupture, and stroke occurred in 3.8% versus 0.8% (p=0.067).
Yes—teaching text comprehension strategies improved general reading comprehension in adults with mild intellectual disability, with substantial transfer effects that were maintained at follow-up.
The study included 38 adults aged 20–72 years (mean age 36) with ID and IQs of 45–69 (mean IQ 58), who received 15 weekly 1-hour lessons over 3 months.
There was no significant difference between individual instruction and small-group reciprocal teaching instruction conditions.
Direct strategy-test effects were substantial except for questioning, and the transfer effect to general text comprehension was even more substantial.

In a retrospective review of 56 patients with nonpalpable testis and spermatic vessels and vas deferens exiting a closed internal inguinal ring, 8 testicular remnants (14%) had viable germ cell elements and 4 (7%) had seminiferous tubules without germ cell elements.
The passages do not compare surgery with observation or report clinical outcomes, so they do not settle whether removal is necessary.

Yes—breast cancer prognosis appears to be inherited, based on a Swedish population-based cohort showing that relatives of women with poor prognosis had worse survival. In 2,787 mother-daughter and 831 sister pairs with breast cancer diagnosed from 1961 to 2001, 5-year survival was 87% among daughters whose mothers died within 5 years versus 91% if the mother was alive (p=0.03), and 70% versus 88% among sisters (p=0.001). After adjustment, daughters and sisters of a proband with poor prognosis had 60% higher 5-year breast cancer mortality than those of a proband with good prognosis (HR 1.6, 95% CI 1.2–2.2; p for trend 0.002), with a slightly stronger association among sisters (HR 1.8) than daughters (HR 1.6).

In a prospective study, 218 preschool children were assigned to either specialized phonological awareness training to prevent dyslexia or general perception training, and 131 were later compared in first grade for reading and writing.
In the whole group, only a slight difference was found between the two training modalities for writing abilities.
However, children with a history of hearing loss, current hearing loss, or pathologic middle ear findings profited most from the specialized program in reading compared with controls.
Yes, routine laboratory markers appear useful for differentiating nonalcoholic from alcoholic steatohepatitis.

In 95 patients with steatohepatitis (58 NASH, 37 ASH), MCV was elevated in 53% of ASH patients but normal in all NASH patients (P<0.0001), and an AST/ALT ratio >1 was more common in ASH (54.1% vs 20.7%, P=0.0008).
Multivariate analysis identified MCV, AST/ALT ratio, and sex as relevant regressors, with an aROC of 0.92.
Yes—pectin content and low-methylated pectin increased with cold acclimation and most cold-induced cell-wall changes were reversed by de-acclimation in winter oil-seed rape.
The evidence comes from leaves of two double-haploid lines of Brassica napus subsp. oleifera differing in winter survival and blackleg resistance.

Cold acclimation at 2°C retarded leaf expansion and increased freezing resistance, leaf tensile stiffness, cell wall and pectin contents, pectin methylesterase activity, and low-methylated pectin content independently of genotype, though changes were more pronounced in the more pathogen-resistant genotype.
De-acclimation promoted leaf expansion and reversed most cold-induced effects except pectin methylesterase activity.

Yes, laparoscopic surgery was associated with a decreased risk of new-onset atrial fibrillation after major foregut surgery in a retrospective study of 154 adults. In that study, 14 of 154 patients developed new-onset atrial fibrillation, and laparoscopic surgery (p = 0.004) and nonthoracic surgery (p = 0.01) were associated with lower risk. Multivariate analysis adjusting for surgery type showed atrial fibrillation was associated with older age (OR 1.08, 95% CI 1.02–1.14, p = 0.01) and inversely associated with laparoscopic surgery (OR 0.09, 95% CI 0.01–0.95, p = 0.04).

The evidence is mixed/insufficient to conclude that it is better to be big, because an evaluation of a Swedish hospital merger found only a moderate quality increase and did not clearly show the hoped-for economic gains.
The evaluation surveyed 597 randomly selected employees (24% of health care staff) at Blekinge Hospital; 498 responded (83%), and interviews were also conducted.
A moderate increase in quality was assessed, but a low proportion of employees perceived it had decisively or largely to do with the merger.
The majority perceived economic incentives as drivers of change, but only 10% of that group believed the target was reached completely or to a large extent.
Yes—adjuvant aromatase inhibitors are associated with a modestly increased risk of grade 3/4 cardiovascular events compared with tamoxifen in early breast cancer trials.

In a meta-analysis of 7 randomized trials including 19,818 patients, the absolute difference in cardiovascular adverse events was 0.52%, with RR 1.31 (95% CI 1.07–1.60; P=.007) and NNH 189; for third-generation AIs, RR was 1.34 (95% CI 1.09–1.63; P=.0038).
The same analysis found thromboembolic events were significantly less frequent with AIs than tamoxifen (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.42–0.65; P<.0001).
The passages do not explicitly state that the trial populations were postmenopausal, although they describe adjuvant AI versus tamoxifen trials in early breast cancer.
No—Kell alloimmunization was not associated with clinically significant fetal thrombocytopenia, although mild thrombocytopenia occurred in 10%.

In a retrospective cohort of 42 pregnancies with severe Kell alloimmunization, fetal thrombocytopenia (platelet count <150 x 10^9/L) was found in 4/42 (10%), compared with 84/318 (26%) in RhD alloimmunized controls.

None of the Kell fetuses, including 15 with severe hydrops, had clinically significant thrombocytopenia (<50 x 10^9/L), whereas 2/230 (1%) non-hydropic and 7/30 (23%) severely hydropic RhD fetuses did.
Thus the evidence does not support an association between Kell alloimmunization and clinically significant fetal thrombocytopenia, though mild thrombocytopenia can occur.

Yes—home sampling kits for multiple bacterial STIs were generally viewed as acceptable among men who have sex with men in a qualitative study, though concerns were raised. The finding rests on focus groups with 20 MSM and one-to-one interviews with 24 MSM, some of whom had experience with self-sampling in a pilot clinical study. Participants identified benefits such as increased access to testing, enhanced personal comfort and empowerment, but also concerns about test accuracy, delays in receiving results, possible lack of support, and potential negative impact on others.
The evidence is insufficient to establish a diagnostic role for c-kit in HBV-related liver disease, because the study reports expression patterns and prevalence but no diagnostic accuracy measures.

In 125 HBV-infected patients grouped as mild, moderate, or severe hepatitis, cirrhosis, and HCC (25 each), plus 50 additional HBV-related HCCs, c-kit immunohistochemistry showed the greatest positivity and staining intensity in severe hepatitis and HCC, with staining intensity paralleling grade and stage in chronic hepatitis B.
C-kit positivity was rare or absent in fibrotic areas and cirrhotic liver, while 62 of 75 HCC specimens (82%) were positive (p<0.001).
These findings show an association with disease severity and HCC but do not settle whether c-kit has diagnostic utility.
Yes, the zeolite hemostatic agent decreased total blood loss in a swine extremity arterial injury model.

In this study, 16 swine with a lacerated femoral artery were allocated to a control group (n=6) treated with a pressure dressing and manual pressure or a QuikClot group (n=10) treated by direct application of QuikClot.
The QuikClot group also had a slower drop in blood pressure and significantly higher hematocrit levels, though the agent generated significant heat and mild nerve changes were observed.

No, the supplied evidence suggests hormonal differences are not responsible for the gender dimorphism: female gender was independently associated with a 43% lower risk of multiple organ failure and a 23% lower risk of nosocomial infection, and this protection remained unchanged in young (<48 years) versus old (>52 years) women.
The cohort included 1,036 blunt-injured adults with hemorrhagic shock (680 men, 356 women) and used Cox regression controlling for confounders.
The passages do not directly measure hormones; they use reproductive age as a proxy and show that the female advantage persists across age groups, arguing against an age-related hormonal explanation.

The evidence is mixed: in a neurovascular clinic cohort, older patients (>75 years) had similar time from symptom onset to clinic appointment (median 24 days vs 24 days) and no differences in prescribed secondary preventive treatments compared with younger patients (≤75 years), but they received less MRI (4% vs 26%) and carotid Doppler imaging (77% vs 92%) and less advice on weight reduction (12.9% vs 30.2%) and diet (31.7% vs 46.3%). Older patients also experienced less delay for carotid endarterectomy (49 vs 90 days), while younger patients had scans performed more quickly. The passages do not define a standard for adequate stroke care or report clinical outcomes, so they cannot fully settle whether older patients receive adequate care overall.

No—on multivariate analysis the growth rate was not related to the neoplastic nature of a gallbladder polyp, although a rapid growth rate (>0.6 mm/mo) was more common in neoplastic polyps univariately.

In 145 patients with GB polyps followed by ultrasound before cholecystectomy (125 non-neoplastic, 20 neoplastic), neoplastic polyps were more frequent with age >60 years, hypertension, size >10 mm, and growth >0.6 mm/mo.
However, only older age (>60 y) and large size (>10 mm) remained significantly associated with neoplastic polyps on multivariate analysis.

No, prostate specific antigen does not appear to need adjustment for body mass index, based on a longitudinal aging study finding no significant association after age adjustment. In 994 men without prostate cancer (4,937 observations), a 10-point BMI increase was associated with a PSA difference of only -0.03 ng/ml (95% CI -0.40-0.49), and the age-adjusted association was not significant (p = 0.06). Results were similar when men with prostate cancer were included, when percent body fat replaced BMI, and after adjusting for prostate volume, and longitudinal weight changes also had no significant association with PSA.
The evidence is insufficient to establish a causative link between probable Say-Barber-Miller syndrome and cerebro-mediastinal tuberculosis.

The report describes a seven-year-old girl with probable Say-Barber-Miller syndrome (facial dysmorphy, microcephaly, mental retardation, recurrent infections) who presented with a mediastinal mass involving the spine and cerebral tuberculomas, with a positive tuberculin reaction and vertebral biopsy culture positive for Koch bacillus.
An extensive immunological work-up was normal, and the authors discuss a putative causative link without comparative or mechanistic evidence.
Thus, the passages show co-occurrence and a hypothesis, but they do not settle whether the syndrome caused the tuberculosis.

In a prospective cohort of 176 patients with PMR followed for 5 years, elevated plasma viscosity (>=2.00 vs <=1.80 mPa s) and starting prednisolone >15 mg independently reduced the probability of stopping steroids within 5 years (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.29-0.82; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.41-0.97).

Late GCA was predicted on univariable analysis by female sex (OR 8.16), HLA-DRB1*0101 or -*0401 alleles (OR 4.95), elevated plasma viscosity (OR 10.64), and initial prednisolone >15 mg (OR 4.53), whereas no significant predictors of relapse were identified.

The evidence is mixed: in a proof-of-concept study, fenofibrate did not significantly reduce the apnoea/hypopnoea index but did improve some secondary sleep apnoea indices. In 34 subjects with mild to moderate sleep apnoea syndrome not treated with continuous positive airways pressure, randomized to fenofibrate 145 mg daily or placebo for 4 weeks, the AHI reduction versus control was 14% (95%CI -47 to 40%, p=0.533). However, fenofibrate significantly reduced the percentage of time with SpO2<90% (from 9.0% to 3.5% vs.
24.0 to 25.0, p=0.004). These exploratory findings are limited by short treatment duration and lack of correction for multiplicity.

Yes, a limited opportunity for rescue antenatal corticosteroids exists, based on the finding that 124 of 692 women (17.9%) remained pregnant 1 week after antenatal corticosteroid administration and delivered before 34 weeks.
In a retrospective analysis of women at 24-32 weeks' gestation who received antenatal corticosteroids, 46.4% delivered within 1 week, including 13.3% within 24 hours.

Women who received antenatal corticosteroids for premature preterm rupture of membranes (OR 3.83, 95% CI 2.06-7.17), twins (OR 2.90, 95% CI 1.42-5.95), or before 28 weeks (OR 2.21, 95% CI 1.38-3.52) were more likely to deliver before 34 weeks.
In 30 guinea pigs divided into control, therapeutic-dose, and double-therapeutic-dose groups, control cochleae showed no changes.
The therapeutic dose caused loss and distortion of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells plus loss of spiral ganglia cells.
The double therapeutic dose distorted inner and outer hair cells and also caused loss of spiral ganglia cells.
The introduction notes that no studies have investigated halofantrine's effect on hearing in humans.

Yes, the evidence suggests ESC can change the way some people drive, based on self-reported long-lasting changes in driving behavior among ESC owners. In a Canadian survey of 1,017 owners/drivers of 2006–2008 ESC-equipped passenger vehicles, 23% of those who knew their vehicle had ESC reported noticing long-lasting changes in their driving behavior since they began driving it. The study also found that 90% of drivers who knew their vehicle had ESC believed it made driving safer and were confident it would work in an emergency, though the objective was to assess whether behavioral adaptation is likely rather than to measure actual driving changes.
Yes, scale matters: the proportion and location of significant racial disparities in breast cancer mortality changed depending on the geographic level and the type of statistic used.

In Texas from 1995-2005, African-American and Hispanic women generally had higher mortality than White non-Hispanic women, with significant disparities especially in southeast metropolitan areas and the southwest border.

Comparing census tract, zip code, and county scales and relative risk (RR) versus risk difference (RD) statistics, the largest proportion of significant results was observed for the RD statistic and census tract data.
Geographic regions with significant disparities for African-Americans and Hispanics frequently had a poverty rate above 10.00%.
Yes, endometrial polyp formation is associated with increased expression of both VEGF and TGF-β1, though the increase is compartment- and phase-specific.

In a prospective study of 70 premenopausal women comparing polyps with adjacent endometrium, VEGF was significantly higher in glandular cells in both proliferative (P<0.001) and secretory (P=0.03) phases and in stromal cells only in the proliferative phase (P=0.006).
TGF-β1 was significantly higher in glandular cells only in the proliferative phase (P=0.02) and in stromal cells in both proliferative (P=0.006) and secretory (P=0.008) phases.
The evidence is mixed: in a cross-sectional study, older cancer patients had specific needs but few significant differences from younger patients, except for intimacy and support.
The study included cancer patients aged 35–82, split into ≤65 and ≥66 years, and assessed needs with the Needs Evaluation Questionnaire.

Older patients most often requested financial-insurance information (73.9%), talking with people with the same illness (71.7%), more comprehensible information from doctors/nurses (71.7%), and better dialogue with clinicians (69.6%), yet only intimacy and support needs differed significantly between age groups.
Yes, the association varies by gender, though the marital-status difference disappears after adjusting for living arrangements.

In the Swiss National Cohort of all residents over age 44 (n=2,440,242), being married benefited men more than women, and among 45–64-year-olds the highest mortality risks were for divorced men living alone (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.67–1.76) and single men living alone (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.63–1.71), whereas women in that age group had the highest risk if single and living with a partner (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.58–1.82).
However, after adjustment for living arrangements, the gender difference by marital status disappeared, and the impact of marital status decreased in older age groups.
Yes—the Turkish EQ-5D showed construct validity in acute coronary syndrome patients, based on its relationships with the MacNew heart-related quality of life scale.
In 122 ACS patients (mean age 62.9±9.3 years; 72.1% male), the EQ-5D index correlated with MacNew subscales at r=0.557–0.721, and the EQ-5D VAS correlated at r=0.297–0.484 (p<0.001 for all).
MacNew global score was also a significant factor for the EQ-5D index (β=0.188; 95% CI 0.152–0.224; p<0.001).

No—delivery mode was not significantly associated with postpartum quality of life in this rural Chinese sample. In a cross-sectional household survey of women 0–12 months after childbirth from 30 rural townships, none of the six quality-of-life dimensions or the total score differed significantly between normal delivery and cesarean section. The cesarean rate was 70.0% (962/1375), with 59.7% of cesareans selected by maternal request; quality of life was instead associated with factors such as postnatal home visit, husband education level, and infant gender.

The evidence is insufficient to say whether mesopic pupil size can be measured with a cobalt blue light slit-lamp biomicroscopy method, because the supplied study describes a slit-lamp biomicroscopy-based method (SLBM) for pupil diameter but does not specify mesopic conditions or cobalt blue light.
It compared SLBM to Colvard infrared pupillometry in 40 healthy eyes, finding mean pupil diameter 5.81 ± 0.70 mm with SLBM vs 6.26 ± 0.68 mm with CIP.
Thus the passages show SLBM can measure pupil diameter but do not settle the specific question about mesopic pupil size using cobalt blue light.
The distribution of health care benefits in Kenya did not meet the principles of universal coverage because benefits were distributed on the basis of ability to pay and not on need for care.

In two nationally representative household surveys from 2003 and 2007, the three sectors had similar pro-rich distribution in 2003, but in 2007 the private-not-for-profit sector was pro-poor, the public sector was equal, and the private-for-profit sector remained pro-rich.
Larger pro-rich disparities were recorded for inpatient compared with outpatient benefits at the hospital level, while primary health care services were pro-poor.
Thus, the evidence shows some pro-poor components but an overall distribution that did not meet universal coverage principles.
Yes, in an in vivo pig model laser pretreatment enhanced transdermal lidocaine absorption.
In four pigs, serum lidocaine and MEGX were undetectable in untreated skin, but both became detectable after Er:YAG laser treatment before topical 4% lidocaine application.
Peak lidocaine was significantly higher at 250 µm (0.62 mg/L) than at 500 µm (0.45 mg/L), 50 µm (0.48 mg/L), or 25 µm (0.3 mg/L).
Peak MEGX was also significantly higher at 250 µm (0.048 mg/L) than at 500 µm (0.018 mg/L), 50 µm (0.036 mg/L), or 25 µm (0.0144 mg/L).
Bottom line: The evidence indicates no consistent correlation between DaTSCAN findings in essential tremor and Parkinson's disease; ET patients typically lack the dopaminergic deficit seen in PD.

In 28 ET patients versus 28 normal volunteers, visual SPECT interpretation showed no uptake differences, while semiquantitative analysis found reduced striatal uptake in ET, and PD patients had reduced putamen uptake.
Clinical follow-up of 20 ET patients showed no signs of PD, and follow-up DaTSCAN in 10 was negative in all but one with an equivocal baseline that deteriorated 12 months later.
Thus, DaTSCAN primarily helps differentiate ET from PD rather than demonstrating a correlation with PD.

Yes—in young obese males, carotid pulsatility and resistance indexes were significantly higher than in healthy controls, supporting them as early sonographic markers of obesity-related vascular dysfunction.

The evidence comes from a study of 35 young obese males and 23 age-matched healthy male volunteers in whom common carotid artery pulsatility index and resistance index were calculated from pulsed Doppler blood flow velocity curves.

Mean pulsatility index and resistance index were statistically higher in obese subjects than controls, alongside higher BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, insulin resistance, and inflammatory markers.

No, the evidence suggests there is little place for ultrasound as a primary diagnostic test for internal derangement of the temporomandibular joint, because static and dynamic high-resolution ultrasound showed considerably lower sensitivity than magnetic resonance imaging.
This finding comes from a study of 40 patients and 20 asymptomatic volunteers, totaling 120 temporomandibular joints, in which ultrasound was compared with magnetic resonance as the reference test.
The study also reported that articular sounds and physical signs were often insufficient, and that ultrasound faced technical difficulties from limited access due to surrounding bone structures.
No - global management at the same centre did not improve results in this retrospective study.

In 45 GM versus 66 SM patients with synchronous liver metastases and colorectal cancer, overall survival was not significantly different (67% vs 51% at 3 years; 35% vs 31% at 5 years), and 5-year disease-free survival was higher with separate management (14% vs 11%, P=0.009).

Global management reduced the mean number of procedures (1.6 vs 2.3, P=0.003) and more often performed the first liver resection during colorectal surgery (62% vs 6%, P<0.0001), but this did not translate into better oncologic outcomes.

Yes, a porcine training model was developed to teach and practice retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy. In 15 piglets, a standard retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy (RPN) training model was performed with three ports, with operative time ranging from 15 to 50 minutes (median 30) and blood loss from 5 to 100 mL (median 20). The experimental learning curve was eight cases, with significant differences between the first eight (group A) and last seven (group B) for peritoneal opening (p = 0.025), operative time (p = 0.0037), and blood loss (p = 0.026). The model simulated the whole procedure from creating the space to nephrectomy completion.

The evidence is mixed and limited to one specialty: in intensive care medicine, open access was associated with a citation advantage in some analyses, but the overall median citation difference was not statistically significant.
Among 161 articles published in Intensive Care Medicine in 2008 (76% non-open access), median citations were 8 (IQR 4-12) for non-open access versus 9 (6-18) for open access (p=0.084).
In the highest citation range (>8), citations were 13 (10-16) versus 18 (13-21) (p=0.008), and average citations per article per month at 30-35 months were 0.28±0.6 versus 0.38±0.7 (p=0.043).
In adjusted analysis, open access status was an independent factor for citation advantage (β=3.618; p=0.006).
Yes, obesity at the start of adolescence was associated with greater wheezing prevalence and persistence, but not with incident wheezing.

In the 1993 Pelotas birth cohort followed from ages 11 to 15 years, obese individuals at 11 years had a 50% higher prevalence of wheezing at 15 years than eutrophic individuals (RR 1.53; 95% CI: 1.14-2.05), and the risk of persistent wheezing was 1.82 (95% CI: 1.30-2.54) after controlling for confounders.
Weight status and skinfolds were not associated with incident wheezing.
Yes, operative treatment was superior to nonoperative treatment for displaced midshaft clavicular fractures in a meta-analysis of four randomized controlled trials.

In 321 patients, operative treatment had lower rates of nonunion (95% CI 0.05–0.43, P=0.0004), malunion (95% CI 0.06–0.34, P<0.00001), and overall complications (95% CI 0.43–0.76, P=0.0001) than nonoperative treatment.

Operative treatment also had lower rates of neurologic symptoms (95% CI 0.20–0.74, P=0.004) and dissatisfaction with appearance (95% CI 0.19–0.65, P=0.001), with improved functional outcomes (P<0.05), although the assessment data were not consistent or standardized.

In a small single-arm phase-2 study of 42 patients receiving oral etoricoxib 90 mg for seven days after cemented primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis, 62% had no heterotopic ossification, 31% had Brooker grade 1, and 7% had Brooker grade 2.
Because the study had no control or comparator group and reported no statistical comparison, these results cannot establish efficacy.
Multivariate analysis showed platelet count was an independent prognostic factor (P=0.013), along with T grade and N staging.

No—based on the supplied pilot data, sternal skin conductance is not supported as a reasonable surrogate for hot flash measurement, because the second prototype showed only 24% concordance between self-reported and device-recorded hot flashes.

In that study, women recorded hot flashes in a prospective diary while wearing SSC devices, and the first prototype yielded no analyzable skin conductance data while the second prototype had a 24% concordance rate.
Sixteen women wore the device for 5 weeks and found it acceptable, though 31% reported interference with daily activities, but this addresses acceptability rather than surrogate accuracy.
The mean CV was 9.4% for CTR02 and 22.9% for patient sera.
The authors state there are no evidence-based medicine data to critically judge solitary kidney vulnerability versus paired kidneys.

In 10 dogs with a solitary kidney versus 10 with paired kidneys subjected to 90 minutes of left renal artery occlusion, solitary-kidney dogs had only a 20% clearance decrease at 1 week and regained basal function from week 2, whereas paired-kidney dogs had more than 90% clearance decrease up to week 2 and still had a 23% reduction at 4 weeks.

Histology showed less tubular necrosis in solitary kidneys (60% at 3 days, regeneration from 1 week) than paired kidneys (90%, regeneration from 2 weeks), and proinflammatory markers were higher and more sustained in paired kidneys.

Yes, lumbar drainage of postoperative CSF fistula after spine surgery appears effective, since all 10 drained patients healed their wounds with no adverse events and cured in a mean of 10 days. The finding comes from 16 of 198 spine surgery patients who developed postoperative CSF fistulas; 6 were treated conservatively with prone positioning for three weeks and 10 with external CSF lumbar drainage for ten days. The drained group cured in a mean of 10 days versus 30 days for conservative treatment, though this is a small series of 16 patients.
No—concomitant anterior/apical repair did not improve the overactive bladder component of mixed incontinence beyond midurethral sling alone in the supplied retrospective cohort.

Among 151 women with bothersome mixed urinary incontinence, 67 underwent MUS-only and 84 underwent MUS plus anterior/apical repair, with the primary outcome being change in OAB-q Symptom Severity at 6 weeks.
OAB-q SS change scores were 30 ± 26 for MUS-only versus 25 ± 25 for MUS + AA (p = 0.20), and multivariate regression also showed no difference between cohorts.

In a prospective study of 87 AMD patients (45 wet, 42 dry) and 80 healthy controls, the HIF1A SNPs rs11549465 and rs11549467 showed no statistically significant difference in genotype distribution between patients and healthy subjects.
The only significant polymorphism association reported was for CFH rs1061170, not HIF1A.
Yes, in vitro: DAC hydrogel combined with various antibacterials showed bactericidal and antibiofilm effects in vitro.
The evidence comes from in vitro spectrophotometry, microbiologic, broth microdilution, and crystal violet assays, with complete release of all tested antibacterial compounds in less than 96 hours.

The passage does not give quantitative reductions in colonization or biofilm or a direct comparison group, and it separately reports that about 80% of the coating was retrieved after press-fit insertion in rabbit tibias and human femurs.
The androgen metabolite ADT-G did not correlate with sexual desire.

The evidence is insufficient to definitively establish that bone thickness and inter-radicular space affect miniscrew placement, but the study reports these as primary outcome variables in the posterior mandible.

In 100 patients (mean age 17.4 ± 6.74 years; 61 female, 39 male; 60 Class I and 40 Class II molar relationships), inter-radicular space ranged from 2.46 to 3.31 mm and alveolar bone thickness ranged from 8.01 to 13.77 mm, with thickness decreasing as insertion angle increased from 45° to 90°.
No significant differences were found between genders or malocclusion types.
No—most elderly patients in this study did not correctly endorse calling 911 for stroke scenarios.
Among 367 out-patients aged ≥60 in Buenos Aires, only 14% correctly endorsed intention to call 911 on the Stroke Action Test using a ≥75% cutoff.
For the most typical stroke signs and symptoms, only 65% reported they would call an ambulance, and the correct response was chosen only 37% of the time on average.
This reflects intended rather than actual 911 calling, and higher education was associated with better endorsement.

Yes—loss of DKK3 expression was associated with lymph node metastasis and, when combined with CT, improved the accuracy of CT staging for predicting lymph node involvement from 71.5% to 80.0% in advanced gastric cancer.
This rests on 158 gastric cancer patients who underwent gastrectomy, in whom DKK3 loss occurred in 64/158 (40.5%) and was associated with lymph node metastasis (p<0.001).
The passage reports the combined prediction in advanced gastric cancer patients using preoperative CT stage, but it does not specify whether DKK3 itself was measured preoperatively.

In 29 schizophrenia patients with exceptionally high pre-morbid intelligence (mean estimated IQ 120), about half also had minimal post-onset IQ decline (<10 points), and they were compared with schizophrenia patients of typical IQ using multinomial logistic regression.

High-IQ patients had significantly lower negative and disorganised symptoms than typical patients (RRR=0.019; 95% CI=0.001–0.675, P=0.030) and better global functioning and insight (RRR=1.082; 95% CI=1.020–1.148; P=0.009).
Those with minimal post-onset IQ decline also showed higher manic symptoms (RRR=8.213; 95% CI=1.042–64.750, P=0.046).

The evidence is insufficient to establish whether vitamin D insufficiency or deficiency is related to the development of osteochondritis dissecans; the supplied study reports a high prevalence of deficiency among OCD patients but provides no comparison group.

In that prospective pilot study, 23 consecutive patients (12 male, 11 female) with stage III or stages III and IV OCD lesions admitted for surgery had serum vitamin D3 measured, and their mean age was 31.3 years.
Among them, 18/23 had a distinct vitamin D3 deficiency, 2 were vitamin D3-insufficient, and 3 reached the lowest normal value.

The study aimed to analyze whether vitamin D insufficiency or deficiency might be a contributing etiological factor, but these descriptive findings alone do not settle whether it is related to development.
Yes—in a retrospective case-control study, ACL reconstruction failure was associated with steeper posterior tibial slopes.
5.5° ± 3.0°, P = 0.006) than controls.
Medial PTS ≥5° had an odds ratio of 6.8 for ACLR failure (P = 0.007), and lateral PTS ≥5° had an odds ratio of 10.8 (P = 0.000).
These findings support an association, but they come from a single small retrospective study and do not by themselves prove causation.

No, the probability of prenatal diagnosis or termination of pregnancy for fetal anomaly was not statistically different between fetuses with congenital heart defects conceived by assisted reproductive techniques (ART) and those conceived spontaneously.

In a population-based Paris study, prenatal diagnosis was 28.1% in ART-conceived (n=171) versus 34.6% in spontaneously conceived (n=4620) fetuses (P=0.077), and termination for fetal anomaly was 36.2% versus 39.2% (P=0.677).
Adjusted estimates were similar, and gestational age at termination was comparable.
This finding is limited to congenital heart defects, not all congenital anomalies.
No, the study found no response to load in either T1DM or control group over the 4 days post exercise.
It compared 7 individuals with T1DM and 10 controls who regularly ran >5 km; baseline tendon structure was similar (UTC echo-types I-IV and anterior-posterior thickness all p > 0.05).
Thus, in this small comparison, T1DM did not affect Achilles tendon response to a 10 km run.
Likely yes: the lifetime model gave an ICER of £482/QALY, below the £30,000/QALY willingness-to-pay threshold, though probabilistic sensitivity analysis showed uncertainty.
This was based on 612 pregnant women in Glasgow randomized to usual cessation support plus or minus up to £400 in vouchers, comparing cotinine-validated quitters, QALYs, and NHS costs.
The incremental cost per quitter at 34–38 weeks was £1127, and the lifetime model found an incremental cost of £17 and a gain of 0.04 QALYs.
The evidence therefore supports cost-effectiveness, but uncertainty—particularly about relapse after birth—means additional research may be worthwhile.

Overall, nurses were not better than the simple objective GAPS score for predicting admission at triage; GAPS and nurses' VAS had comparable discrimination (AUC 0.876 vs 0.875, p=0.93) and binary accuracy (80.6% vs 79.0%, p=0.18), while nurses overestimated admissions (47.3% vs observed 40.7%, p<0.0001).

In the majority of attendances where nurses were less than 95% certain, GAPS significantly outperformed nurses on calibration (+1.2% vs +9.2%, p<0.0001), discrimination (AUC 0.810 vs 0.759, p=0.001), and accuracy (75.1% vs 68.9%, p=0.0009).

When nurses felt at least 95% certain, their VAS accuracy was excellent at 92.4%, and a strategy using GAPS but over-ruling it with ≥95% clinical certainty outperformed either method alone (AUC 0.891, accuracy 82.5%).
The evidence is insufficient to establish obesity as the triggering cause of incidentally detected idiopathic misty mesentery, although the study reports a high obesity prevalence in this population.

Among 561 patients with misty mesentery on abdominopelvic CT, 80 had isolated incidental idiopathic misty mesentery, a prevalence of 7%, and 67.5% of all patients were obese while 17.5% were overweight.
No, viral co-infection did not influence the severity of acute respiratory infection in children; the number of detected viruses did not correlate with any markers of severity.
This finding came from 204 children admitted with acute respiratory infection in a Spanish prospective multicenter study (2011-2013) and was replicated in an independent UK cohort of 97 children.

In contrast, bacterial superinfection was associated with increased severity (OR 4.356, P=0.005), PICU admission (OR 3.342, P=0.006), higher clinical score (1.988, P=0.002), respiratory support (OR 7.484, P<0.001), and longer hospital length of stay (OR 1.468, P<0.001).

In patients undergoing open ventral hernia repair followed for at least 1 month, across a retrospective multicenter database (n=795; SSO rate 23%) and a single-center prospective database (n=88; SSO rate 14%), the tested models (VHRS, VHWG, CDC Wound Class, HW-RAT, and, in the prospective cohort, ACS-NSQIP) had low AUCs for SSO, ranging from 0.50 to 0.60 in the retrospective database and 0.50 to 0.69 in the prospective database.

Although VHRS and HW-RAT significantly stratified SSO in the retrospective database and ACS-NSQIP did so in the prospective database, the models also systematically over- or underestimated SSO risk, so the passages show limited accuracy rather than reliable prediction.

Yes, the evidence suggests that aortic arch anatomy influences aortic trauma severity, with the aortic arch angle significantly associated with type III damage in a retrospective series. That study included 22 patients treated with TEVAR for traumatic aortic injury from 2009 to 2014 and classified injury severity according to Society of Vascular Surgery recommendations. Mean aortic arch index and angle were 6.8 cm and 58.3° for type I, 4.4 cm and 45.9° for type III, and 3.3 cm and 37° for type IV, with substantial differences between type III and IV groups. Multivariate analysis confirmed the aortic arch angle was significantly associated with type III damage (OR 1.5; 95% CI 1.03-2.2). However, these findings come from only 22 cases in one department, so they are limited.
Yes—qualitative findings suggest MPH programs can contribute to health system strengthening in low- and middle-income countries, mainly through workplace and policy impacts.

In a six-country mixed-methods study focused on two English-language MPH programs (a distance program from South Africa and a residential program in the Netherlands), 10 graduates per program working in low- and middle-income health systems, plus their peers and supervisors, reported considerable workplace impact.

Reported contributions included promotion to leadership positions, expanded or revitalized management roles, workplace innovations, teaching and training, advocacy, community engagement, and national-level policy advisory roles, policy development, and capacity building.
However, these findings are qualitative and context-dependent, with work conditions influencing impact and possible self-selection, untraceable graduates, and social acceptability bias.
Yes—the retromandibular transparotid approach appeared safe and reliable for surgical treatment of condylar fractures in a retrospective series of 25 patients.
In that study, preinjury occlusion and temporomandibular joint health were restored in most patients, and esthetic outcomes were satisfactory to clinicians and patients.
Neither permanent neurologic impairments nor major postoperative complications were observed.
However, this was a single retrospective evaluation without a stated comparator, so it supports reliability but does not definitively compare the approach with others.
Yes—populations with access to general practitioner hospitals had lower general hospital utilisation, with 38% and 52% fewer occupied bed days for men and women, though the evidence is observational.

In the Finnmark study, total general hospital admission rates were 26% lower for men and 28% lower for women in peripheral municipalities with a GP hospital than in central municipalities without one.
Because this was an observational comparison, it shows an association and does not by itself prove that GP hospitals cause the reduction.

In 55 potential brain-dead donors evaluated by TEE, 20 had FAC <50%, and 40 hearts were harvested, 36 successfully transplanted; among recipients, 9 had donor FAC <50% (group H2) and 27 had donor FAC >50% (group H1).

Four recipients died, including one from right and one from left ventricular dysfunction with donor FAC <50%, while donor FAC increased from 51 +/- 15% to 57 +/- 11% in 18 hearts assessed in donors and later recipients.

Actuarial survival was 86.2% versus 64.6% at 1 and 2 years in group H1 versus group H2, respectively, but the difference was not statistically significant (p = NS), so these data do not definitively settle suitability.
